title: Google says Russian speakers pulled off first-ever fully automated AI cyberattack
content:
Russian-speaking hackers built an AI agent that carried out what may be the first-ever fully-automated cyberattack, Google reported Monday.

The tech giant’s cyber threat intelligence division said it had spotted hackers using artificial intelligence to “fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop for the first time.”

The development could mark an inflection point in the use of AI for cyberattacks, which has dominated headlines and worried policymakers since AI firm Anthropic released its specialized model Mythos in April. 

Hackers, who used Russian in technical documentation identified by Google, set up a series of AI agents to “continuously compare pre- and post-patch code, identify vulnerabilities, and automatically develop exploits without human intervention,” Google said.

That means the agents independently found software flaws and ways to use them. The attackers targeted French websites in the media, entertainment and education sectors, Google said.
snippet: Russian-speaking hackers built an AI agent that carried out what may be the first-ever fully-automated cyberattack, Google reported Monday.
creator: Sam Clark

title: EU sanctions Russian trolls, hackers
content:
European Union member countries on Monday issued sanctions against a Russian company running disinformation campaigns and one of Russia’s most well-known hacking groups.

The Council of the EU said it had sanctioned the Social Design Agency, a Moscow-based firm that carries out “large scale information manipulation and interference projects,” as well as 24 of its staff members.

The Social Design Agency is “funded, directed and supervised” by the Russian government and has organized disinformation campaigns targeting EU countries, EU institutions and European support for Ukraine, Council said.

The group has been connected in the past to a vast online disinformation network known as Doppelganger. It targeted the 2024 European elections and carried out “dedicated operations against EU member states such as Germany and France,” countries said.

EU capitals also agreed to levy sanctions against notorious Russian hacking group NoName057(16), which has targeted government bodies and critical infrastructure as well as private firms in the EU, Ukraine and the United States.
snippet: European Union member countries on Monday issued sanctions against a Russian company running disinformation campaigns and one of Russia’s most well-known hacking groups.
creator: Sam Clark

title: Estonia has a plan for Russian occupation: Run its government from the cloud
content:
TALLINN — Imagine French General Charles de Gaulle, exiled in London during World War II, running his Free France government by logging into the cloud.

Officials in Estonia are preparing for exactly such a scenario with a new strategy to boost doomsday resilience — hukukindlus in Estonian — that would allow the government’s digital services to be run entirely from abroad if its territory is occupied by a foreign enemy.

The Baltic country of  1.3 million, which shares a 294-kilometer border with Russia, fears it is a prime target if Moscow were to invade a European Union country. Security services have already warned that Russia is waging a hybrid war on Europe, and Estonia has blamed Moscow for everything from cyberattacks to arson plots to cuts to undersea data cables.

Now, Tallinn is preparing to move its public services to the cloud “either when data centers are destroyed or there’s boots on the ground and we cannot operate,” said Tõnu Grünberg, an architect of the new strategy and former deputy secretary general for digital infrastructure and cybersecurity at Estonia’s Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs.
snippet: TALLINN — Imagine French General Charles de Gaulle, exiled in London during World War II, running his Free France government by logging into the cloud.
creator: Laurens Cerulus, Ellen O'Regan

title: The EU has always found a way through. On AI, it’s struggling to see it.
content:
There might be an AI apocalypse. European leaders don’t really want to talk about it.

By SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC and PIETER HAECK
in DUBLIN

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

The European Union wasn’t set up to deal with challenges as vast and existential as the possibility of AI wiping out humanity.

For two decades, the EU’s leaders have muddled through crisis after crisis — from Greece coming within days of being pushed out of the eurozone, to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, which forced millions to seek safety in the bloc. Each time, it has found a way through. It’s what the EU does.

With AI, though, it’s turning out to be different.

Tech experts, industry and even governments themselves describe paralysis, distraction and defeatism in Europe’s capitals. It’s telling that it took four years after the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022 for EU leaders to bring themselves to discuss artificial intelligence at a summit in Dublin on Friday.

And even then, there was little enthusiasm for the topic.
snippet:
There might be an AI apocalypse. European leaders don’t really want to talk about it.

By SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC and PIETER HAECKin DUBLIN

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO
creator: Sebastian Starcevic, Pieter Haeck

title: Italy hits Meta with €805M fine over privacy law violation
content:
Italian authorities fined Facebook’s parent company Meta €805 million for using photos and videos from Android phones without users’ specific consent, the Italian Data Protection Authority said in a statement Saturday. 

The fine concerned the “camera roll suggestions when browsing Facebook” feature, which suggests photos and videos from a phone’s gallery for users to add to posts.

The feature violates the Italian law implementing the EU’s ePrivacy directive, the authority said. It is by far the largest fine ever imposed by the Italian regulator.

The investigation, launched in 2025, established that access to a user’s camera roll is requested with a single permission for the entire app, which the authority said covers multiple features with different needs. The authorization request was preceded by a generic warning that didn’t allow users to understand that they were authorizing picture and video suggestions, the authority said. 

“If granted in full, this type of permission allows the app to read the device’s entire photo archive, usually permanently, without the user or the authorities being able to verify which information is actually being used,” the statement reads.

title: EU deal on Ukraine talks overshadows AI-focused summit in Dublin
content:
They came to discuss AI, but EU leaders spent most of their time during a summit in Dublin on Friday grappling with questions about Ukraine — namely who should represent them in future peace talks.

Despite plenty of disagreement about whether it should be a single person (and if so, who) or a collection of them, they managed to strike a deal: Future talks would involve national security officials from Germany, France, the U.K., Italy and Poland — the so-called E5 powers — plus representatives from the European Commission and European Council. A classic European compromise.

“It is essential to have a team and to speak with one voice,” European Council President António Costa said after the summit, noting that Donald Trump had also tasked two envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, with conducting negotiations.

Ireland, which holds the EU’s rotating presidency and hosted the informal gathering, had billed the meeting as a rare chance for a high-level discussion on how to develop artificial intelligence in accordance with European values.
snippet: They came to discuss AI, but EU leaders spent most of their time during a summit in Dublin on Friday grappling with questions about Ukraine — namely who should represent them in future peace talks.
creator: Nicholas Vinocur, Jacopo Barigazzi, Hans von der Burchard

title: Microsoft outage renews European calls to detox from US tech
content:
DUBLIN — Friday’s widespread outage of Microsoft products has sparked a new wave of calls for Europe to control its own digital infrastructure — especially with the uncertain future of artificial intelligence at stake.

“Only 20% of European digital services run on European infrastructure,” Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch said in remarks Friday after he addressed EU national leaders during their first-ever meeting on artificial intelligence in Dublin.

The money spent on foreign, U.S. or Chinese, technology “could be reinvested here, on infrastructure we control and [to] finance European research and development,” said the boss of Europe’s leading AI frontier lab.

Mensch didn’t specifically address the Microsoft outage, which lasted nearly 24 hours and affected millions of users in 74 countries. Still, the shutdown of key tools like Outlook email and Teams messaging impacted plenty of the tech and government leaders gathered in Dublin to chart Europe’s AI future.

creator: Pieter Haeck

title: EU institutions survive Microsoft outage unscathed
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union institutions kept calm and carried on regulating on Friday, as many other parts of the world muttered at their computers over a massive digital outage at U.S. tech leader Microsoft.

The European Commission, Council of the EU and European Parliament were able to carry on business as usual, with systems remaining largely unaffected.

Microsoft’s global outage, which disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot started on Thursday, with internet traffic monitoring site Downdetector reporting issues in at least 74 countries. The tracker logged nearly 140,000 reports of Outlook problems at its peak.

Microsoft on Friday morning said recovery was still uneven. “At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation,” it said.

At the European Commission “the impact … is very limited and does not affect our operations,” spokesperson Thomas Regnier told POLITICO. He said the outage had a “minor impact on a limited number of applications, such as the slowness of SharePoint.” Outlook and Teams were “fully operational,” Regnier said.
snippet: BRUSSELS — The European Union institutions kept calm and carried on regulating on Friday, as many other parts of the world muttered at their computers over a massive digital outage at U.S. tech leader
creator: Milena Wälde, Jasper Bennink

title: Tinder owner hit with €11M privacy fine
content:
Ireland’s privacy regulator has fined Tinder owner Match Group €11 million, saying the dating app failed to give users a full copy of their personal data upon request.

The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) said on Friday that a tool Tinder provides to users who want to download their personal data is not up to scratch. The DPC had launched an inquiry in January 2020, focusing on whether Tinder’s “Download My Data” tool is complaint with the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation.

In a decision announced Friday, the DPC said the tool failed to provide users with all of their personal data, and that certain categories of information were omitted, or users were only given a summary of their data.

The regulator said the tool did not meet requirements set out in the GDPR, that people have a right to access the personal data about them that a company holds.

Deputy Commissioner at the Irish DPC, Graham Doyle, said automated access tools “can be a useful and efficient way” to give people access to their personal data, but they “must be fair and transparent to individuals regarding the extent of the data provided.”
snippet: Ireland’s privacy regulator has fined Tinder owner Match Group €11 million, saying the dating app failed to give users a full copy of their personal data upon request.
creator: Ellen O'Regan

title: Jensen Huang’s fall further exposes EU leaders on AI
content:
BRUSSELS — It takes an 80-year-old German diplomat to put the Jensen Huang spy scandal in proper historical context. 

Asked about allegations that the Nvidia CEO was lured into an intimate relationship with a Chinese spy, Wolfgang Ischinger, Germany’s former ambassador to Washington, pointed to the past. “In World War I, you had female spies who used the honey trap to talk to a general, and maybe sleep with him and extract some secrets,” he told POLITICO.

As Europe’s 27 leaders meet for their first conversation on AI the day after Huang’s resignation, his fall from grace is a reminder that it’s American tech bros — not European military men — who now hold the secrets that can decide the fate of the world.

Friday’s roundtable of European leaders in Dublin must reckon with the reality that the pursuit of AI superiority remains a two-horse race between the U.S. and China — and that Nvidia’s leadership drama doesn’t change the fact that a single American company’s chips will continue to drive the artificial intelligence boom.
snippet: BRUSSELS — It takes an 80-year-old German diplomat to put the Jensen Huang spy scandal in proper historical context.
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: Ukraine Starlink speed restrictions in effect again, Zelenskyy says
content:
KYIV – Limitations affecting Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite system, appear to be back in Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday.

“Unfortunately, our units have been recording significant disruptions to Starshield’s operations over the territory of Ukraine for several days now – along the entire front line and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said in a statement.

About a month ago, Ukraine reported a drop in connectivity for objects traveling faster than 161 km/h, which prevented its defensive systems, especially its interceptors, from working properly. The restriction was lifted on Oct. 24. In his statement, Zelenskyy said the disruptions were not due to a malfunction, but once again to a systematic speed restriction.

“For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones,” Zelenskyy said.

The latest restrictions have already allowed several Russian drones to get through Ukrainian air defense and kill more Ukrainians, he added.
snippet: KYIV – Limitations affecting Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite system, appear to be back in Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday.
creator: Veronika Melkozerova

title: Australia signs up to EU’s Horizon Europe research program
content:
BRUSSELS — Australia’s Industry Minister Tim Ayres formally signed the country up to Horizon Europe on Thursday, giving the country’s researchers access to the EU’s €95 billion research and innovation program.

Australia will join Pillar II of the program, which funds research into areas including advanced computing tech, critical minerals, health, climate and clean energy. From January, Australian organizations will be eligible for funding on the same terms as EU countries and will be able to lead project consortia.

The move will be a “boon for Australian science, research and innovation,” Ayres said in a statement, adding that “the big challenges facing Australia and the world cannot be solved by any one country working alone.”

The signing formalizes negotiations concluded in June. Australian organizations have already taken part in 239 Horizon Europe projects, with nearly one in four applications selected, according to the European Commission.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Australia’s Industry Minister Tim Ayres formally signed the country up to Horizon Europe on Thursday, giving the country’s researchers access to the EU’s €95 billion research and innovation
creator: Zoya Sheftalovich

title: Ahead of Spanish election, Sánchez takes aim at TikTok
content:
MADRID — Trailing in the polls ahead of Nov. 29 national elections, Spain’s ruling Socialist Party is turning to TikTok. Not to use it, but to try to ban it. 

Following the publication on Monday of a Spanish investigation accusing TikTok of allowing child sexual abuse material, the youth ministry announced it would try to block the platform.

On Wednesday the prosecutor’s office opened a preliminary inquiry, prompting a triumphant post on X by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. “Great news,” he wrote. “The days of impunity on social media are over. No platform is above the law, and much less above the rights of our children.”

The bombshell report by civil society group Maldita has shocked Spain and given the government a chance to show it’s tough on Big Tech just ahead of a momentous election, with polls showing the right firmly ahead.

Over the past 72 hours the government has pulled every available legal lever against TikTok, including lodging cases with both the Data Protection Agency and the public prosecutor’s office.
snippet: MADRID — Trailing in the polls ahead of Nov. 29 national elections, Spain’s ruling Socialist Party is turning to TikTok. Not to use it, but to try to ban it.
creator: Nacho Alarcón, Eliza Gkritsi, Ellen O'Regan

title: EU needs a system to respond to AI incidents, Finland and Estonia say
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union should have a plan to respond to serious artificial intelligence incidents, two EU countries said ahead of a key Friday meeting of national leaders focused on AI.

In a letter seen by POLITICO, Finland and Estonia say the bloc “can still compete at the frontier” of AI by mobilizing capital and building up compute power, but this should go hand in hand with “governing it responsibly.”

The two countries, considered among Europe’s digital leaders, call for “EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents.”

AI safety and security are on Friday’s agenda of the first-ever European Council meeting devoted to the revolutionary new technology.

Concerns about whether Europe is prepared to respond to AI-powered threats have been picking up steam since a series of incidents this summer in which AI agents went rogue and hacked into other companies. Recent cyberattacks and revelations of coding vulnerabilities have also raised concerns that security systems must be better equipped for the arrival of artificial intelligence.
snippet: BRUSSELS — The European Union should have a plan to respond to serious artificial intelligence incidents, two EU countries said ahead of a key Friday meeting of national leaders focused on AI.
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: European gaming firms say new EU consumer rules will ‘cripple’ the industry
content:
BRUSSELS — Top global gaming companies have blasted new EU consumer regulations they say would “cripple the competitiveness of Europe’s world-leading video games industry.”

The European Commission unveiled a new set of rules Wednesday on consumer protection, including the Digital Fairness Act, that is part of the first-ever sector-specific limits on the video-game industry, alongside the EU’s mid-September regulation to protect children online.

Under the proposed DFA, which still has to be negotiated with other EU institutions, video games would no longer be able to earn money by offering minors micro-transactions to advance in the game, known as pay-to-win or pay-to-progress. There are also restrictions on “loot boxes,” which contain surprise virtual items that players can buy with real money. The law also stipulates that in-app virtual currencies must be turned off by default for under-18s.

The Commission says these practices encourage overspending, which is especially dangerous for vulnerable consumers like kids. Violating the rules can lead to fines of up to 6% of global revenue in cases that affect more than two-thirds of the EU population.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Top global gaming companies have blasted new EU consumer regulations they say would “cripple the competitiveness of Europe’s world-leading video games industry.”
creator: Eliza Gkritsi

title: Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton for Jensen Huang investigation
content:
Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into reports that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

Law firm partner Joon H. Kim will lead the probe. Kim, a former acting attorney of the Southern District of New York, was appointed in 2021 as an independent investigator by New York Attorney General Letitia James to probe allegations of sexual harassment by former Gov. Andrew Cuomo.

The company’s board of directors on Sunday launched an independent investigation into Jensen Huang following reports of his romantic relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy. The board said that Jensen Huang supports the review.

Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang was first brought to light in an October New York Times report, which alleged the businesswoman had ties to Chinese intelligence. Officials suspected Alice Huang helped funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China, according to the report.

Jensen Huang in a message to the company Sunday admitted to an affair and pledged to cooperate with the investigation. He did not mention Alice Huang by name.
snippet: Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation into reports that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.
creator: Katherine Long

title: Brussels takes on the evils of online commerce
content:
BRUSSELS — You know that customer-service bot that won’t let you cancel your subscription? The EU wants to kill it.  

With a new law presented Wednesday, the European Commission will take aim at the endless array of practices websites have used over the past 20 years to make more money from consumers.  

The Digital Fairness Act is the European response to a wider regulatory trend that has seen consumer authorities curb irksome and exploitative practices. These include dynamic pricing that changes ticket prices based on demand, cumbersome processes for canceling subscriptions and the near-complete surrender of customer service to automated systems.  

According to a draft of the DFA obtained by POLITICO, the Commission will address several aspects of the design, service and terms under which businesses interact with consumers online. 

“Europe should not accept a digital economy where profits depend on exploiting people’s vulnerabilities,” Spanish socialist lawmaker Laura Ballarín Cereza, a key European lawmaker on tech legislation, said in a statement.
snippet: BRUSSELS — You know that customer-service bot that won’t let you cancel your subscription? The EU wants to kill it.
creator: Eliza Gkritsi

title: EU watchdog probes Commission’s AI pick over conflict of interest concerns
content:
The EU’s watchdog is investigating whether the European Commission managed to “identify, assess and address” actual or potential conflicts of interest when it appointed the chairman of Siemens as Ursula von der Leyen’s AI envoy.

A group of NGOs complained in June to the European Ombudsman about the choice of Jim Hagemann Snabe. Among his responsibilities in the role is to produce a report on issues including AI infrastructure, frontier AI technologies and industrial AI adoption. 

The NGOs, which include Transparency International and Corporate Europe Observatory, warned that Snabe’s ongoing role at Siemens “may compromise the envoy’s independence and impartiality.”

The European Ombudsman in September launched a probe into the Commission over its failure to respond to the NGO concerns.

Now, it has gone one step further.

“You argue that the Commission did not properly identify, assess, and address actual or potential conflicts of interest,” Ombudsman Teresa Anjinho wrote in a letter to Corporate Europe Observatory. “Therefore you would like the Commission to revoke the appointment.”
snippet: The EU’s watchdog is investigating whether the European Commission managed to “identify, assess and address” actual or potential conflicts of interest when it appointed the chairman of Siemens as
creator: Mari Eccles

title: EU needs only ‘very trusted partners’ on AI chips, tech chief says amid Nvidia crisis
content:
LISBON — The European Union should work “only with very trusted partners” on artificial intelligence microchips, its tech chief said Tuesday, just days after revelations of a spy scandal rocked industry leader Nvidia.

“When we speak about very critical technologies, like AI semiconductors and quantum technologies, cybersecurity, satellites … it’s very important that we are working very closely only with very trusted partners,” said Henna Virkkunen, the European Commission’s executive vice president for tech sovereignty. She made the comments in an interview with POLITICO at the Web Summit tech fair in Lisbon, when asked about Europe’s reliance on Nvidia.

It is Virkkunen’s first public comment since Nvidia opened an internal investigation into whether its CEO was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation. Top executive Jensen Huang admitted to an affair following a reported relationship with an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed whom the U.S. government believes is a Chinese spy.

creator: Pieter Haeck, Laura Greenhalgh

title: Prince Harry slams ‘lawless’ social media’s impact on children
content:
BRUSSELS — Royalty descended on the European Parliament on Tuesday as Prince Harry slammed Big Tech for creating a world of “chaos.”

“A handful of very powerful people … would like to see the world as a social media world: lawless, no consequence, complete chaos, division,” the Duke of Sussex said at an event on online safety for children.

Speaking in a room packed to the brim with journalists and photographers, Harry called for stricter rules on social media platforms to protect kids from content that could lead to suicide or self-harm.

He expressed reservations about the privacy policies of social media platforms, which he said bar parents from knowing how their children died. “That cannot be right,” a visibly upset Harry said.

His wife, Meghan Markle, was present but withdrew from an address on Tuesday’s panel.

The European Commission regulates online platforms through its Digital Services Act and is planning a special regime for minors under the Kids Act.

The burden of proof that platforms are safe should be on the companies rather than on parents, and “the EU Kids Act is exactly that,” said the prince, praising an EU proposal that would bar access to social media for under-13s.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Royalty descended on the European Parliament on Tuesday as Prince Harry slammed Big Tech for creating a world of “chaos.”
creator: Eliza Gkritsi

title: Europe needs Nvidia. It’ll take more than a spy scandal to change that.
content:
BRUSSELS — Last month, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang got Europe’s full red-carpet treatment from the likes of King Charles, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

Now it’s crickets.

As an alleged Chinese spy scandal engulfs the man running the world’s dominant AI microchips producer, potentially awkward questions loom for European leaders in both the public and private sectors who rubbed shoulders and inked deals with Huang. But the silence also reflects the cold economic and strategic reality that Europe has no homegrown alternative to Nvidia.

A German government spokesperson said Monday in response to a barrage of questions on the upheaval at Nvidia that it “does not comment on the media reports,” and that “we always adhere to the highest standards, including when agreements are being reached.” A European Commission spokesperson also had no comment on the matter.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Last month, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang got Europe’s full red-carpet treatment from the likes of King Charles, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: Spain’s conservatives promise to relax climate rules if they win election
content:
MADRID — Spain’s center-right People’s Party has pledged to “put a stop to the imposition of unrealistic timelines” for climate goals if it wins the national elections on Nov. 29, a significant pivot from the Sánchez government’s pro-green policies.

The PP, the favorite to win the vote, said decarbonization is an “essential goal for Europe,” but promised to push for an “orderly, realistic, and fair transition,” according to the energy chapter of the party’s manifesto obtained by POLITICO’s Madrid Playbook.

The manifesto said it’s time “to reassess the pace of progress” in the clean energy transition “without dogmatism,” while conceding there are “environmental, geostrategic and economic reasons” behind the decarbonization strategy.

Spain under Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has been one of the bloc’s most influential cheerleaders for ambitious climate goals, advocating to protect key EU policies like the Emissions Trading System, pollution reduction targets and the phase-out of gasoline cars.

But the PP’s manifesto shows that would change if the EU’s fourth-largest economy votes for a conservative government led by PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo.
snippet: MADRID — Spain’s center-right People’s Party has pledged to “put a stop to the imposition of unrealistic timelines” for climate goals if it wins the national elections on Nov. 29, a significant pivot
creator: Nacho Alarcón, Diego Rodríguez Veiga

title: AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio implores Europe to build frontier models
content:
BERLIN — Europe must build its own proprietary frontier models of artificial intelligence to avoid risks in relying on U.S. or Chinese models, world-leading AI developer Yoshua Bengio told POLITICO.

Working with open-weight AI models, built in China or elsewhere, would be a dangerous strategy for European companies and governments, locking in long-term economic and military dependence and multiplying cyberattacks, Bengio said.

The European Union is currently locked in a debate about whether to invest the billions necessary for homegrown frontier models, or to build applications on top of proprietary American or open-weight Chinese AI.

“Adapting models you don’t control and you may not have doesn’t work,” said the French-born Canadian computer scientist, who has been vocal in warning about the risks of the breakthrough technology that is largely based on the neural network systems he helped develop.

Asked whether that meant Europe needed to develop its own advanced models, Bengio’s answer was unequivocal: “Of course, because they are the key to everything.”
snippet: BERLIN — Europe must build its own proprietary frontier models of artificial intelligence to avoid risks in relying on U.S. or Chinese models, world-leading AI developer Yoshua Bengio told POLITICO.
creator: Larissa Kögl

title: EU countries still can’t get it together on AI
content:
BRUSSELS — As European leaders prepare to project urgency at their first joint meeting on artificial intelligence, their governments are missing important AI safety and infrastructure targets.

The bloc’s 27 leaders are meeting Friday in Dublin to discuss how to accelerate efforts to stay safe and be more competitive on artificial intelligence.

Yet 16 capitals have missed a deadline to appoint a national authority to enforce the bloc’s AI safety law, and Brussels has also pushed back an effort to support the buildout of data centers because of national administrative delays.

European Parliament lawmaker Sergey Lagodinsky, a German member of the Greens, said the delays are undermining capitals’ credibility when speaking about Europe’s AI ambitions.

“Stop blaming the EU for missing the race if you miss your own deadlines,” he said. “Europe’s AI ambitions cannot be delivered if national capitals cannot get their act together.”

In a letter seen by POLITICO, Lagodinsky asked the European Commission to start a formal procedure against capitals for failing to meet their legal requirements under the AI law.
snippet: BRUSSELS — As European leaders prepare to project urgency at their first joint meeting on artificial intelligence, their governments are missing important AI safety and infrastructure targets.
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: Mélenchon squares up to Brussels in election manifesto
content:
PARIS — French leftist presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon wants a radical overhaul of EU rules that would set him on a collision course with Brussels.

The far-left leader, who has enjoyed a recent surge in the polls ahead of the 2027 election, pitched a series of measures to fundamentally rethink the EU’s agenda in his presidential platform unveiled Friday. Mélenchon also said he would disobey current EU rules that would prevent him from implementing his platform if elected.

Proposing a “new deal” for Europe, Mélenchon wants to redraft the treaties, ditch core parts of the EU’s rulebook — including debt and deficit limits — suspend competition rules for public services such as energy, transport and telecoms, and loosen state aid laws.

“We will immediately implement our program at the national level. This will therefore require a confrontation with European institutions,” according to the manifesto from Mélenchon’s France Unbowed. “This also means disobeying rules blocking [us] whenever necessary.”
snippet: PARIS — French leftist presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon wants a radical overhaul of EU rules that would set him on a collision course with Brussels.
creator: Marion Solletty

title: EU accuses TikTok of designing algorithm that creates ‘rabbit holes’
content:
The European Commission has accused TikTok of violating its online platforms rules for having designed algorithms that lead users down so-called rabbit holes.

The preliminary findings announced Friday mark the first time the Commission has focused on a social media platform’s recommender systems as a breach of its powerful Digital Services Act, under which it can issue fines up to 6% of a company’s annual global revenue.

“This is the first time that we are really tackling head-on the engagement-based recommender system model,” said one Commission official, who was granted speaking anonymity to speak freely.

This is the fifth case of the EU executive accusing TikTok of breaching EU rules, even though it has issued no fines against the Chinese-owned platform.

In Friday’s announcement, the Commission says the company didn’t adequately consider the risk of sending users down “rabbit holes” through a “continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image.”

The investigation focused on mental health impacts because “the evidence was strongest,” when asked about how these rabbit holes contribute to radicalization, said another official.
snippet: The European Commission has accused TikTok of violating its online platforms rules for having designed algorithms that lead users down so-called rabbit holes.
creator: Eliza Gkritsi

title: France, US clash over G7 effort on AI safety
content:
The U.S. government has scuttled a French push for the G7 to coordinate on advanced AI safety, with a White House official calling it “unnecessary bureaucracy.”

France’s digital minister Anne Le Hénanff told a French Senate hearing on Wednesday that she held two ministerial meetings in September and October to secure G7 commitments to a high-level working group to test frontier AI — the most advanced models — and share information about risks and incidents.

That effort “did not reach a successful conclusion” because the U.S. wanted to pursue its own approach, the French minister said.

“They are not prepared, at this stage, to issue a joint statement with the other six G7 nations, and have asked us to wait for the findings of their own assessment,” said Le Hénanff. “Naturally, we regret this, but we are continuing to move forward as Europeans on this issue.”

A White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said that the French government proposed a “poorly defined body” to cooperate on AI that the administration feared would “create unnecessary bureaucracy.”
snippet: The U.S. government has scuttled a French push for the G7 to coordinate on advanced AI safety, with a White House official calling it “unnecessary bureaucracy.”
creator: Milena Wälde, Brendan Bordelon, Émile Marzolf

title: Mélenchon’s mission for his young fans: Debate boomers on Facebook
content:
PARIS — Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s campaign has a plan for winning over older French voters: get his young supporters to sign up for Facebook to talk to their parents.

Mélenchon, 75, may be the oldest candidate in next spring’s race to replace Emmanuel Macron. But his progressive platform and call for a civic revolution have made him a hit with younger voters, who are more likely to scroll through TikTok and Snapchat than through the old-school social network.

“We’re strong [on every other social media platform],” said Antoine Léaument, who handles the Mélenchon campaign’s communication operations. “Facebook is one of the places where the digital battle could be decisive.”

More than 40% of voters younger than 35 plan to vote for Mélenchon, according to a recent Cluster17 poll commissioned by POLITICO. That figure drops to 14% or less across the age brackets over 50 — groups that, if they use social media at all, tend to favor Facebook over its newer rivals.

According to Médiamétrie, France’s leading audience measurement company, platforms like Instagram and Snapchat have 35% more daily users than Facebook among 15-to-24-year-olds.
snippet: PARIS — Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s campaign has a plan for winning over older French voters: get his young supporters to sign up for Facebook to talk to their parents.
creator: Victor Goury-Laffont

title: EU budget battle paralyzes Brussels on AI chips, the Arctic and agriculture
content:
BRUSSELS — Europe’s push to accelerate AI chip production and plan to strengthen its Arctic presence are among the key EU policy files caught in the logjam of Brussels’ seven-year budget standoff.

European policymakers say they can’t move forward on their files without sufficient visibility on proposals linked to EU funding, as the negotiating impasse over the size of the EU’s 2028-2034 budget means financial allocations after next year are unknown.

“There’s an increase in sectoral legislation with objectives that require multiannual budgetary commitments,” said a person involved in talks on the EU budget, who was granted anonymity to discuss closed-door negotiations. “But the budget talks are disconnected from the policy discussions.”

EU governments are racing to find a deal among themselves over the total size of the money pot by the end of the year. The so-called frugal countries pushing for major budget cuts — Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Finland — have publicly said that a proposal by the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU envisioning €159 billion cuts doesn’t go far enough.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Europe’s push to accelerate AI chip production and plan to strengthen its Arctic presence are among the key EU policy files caught in the logjam of Brussels’ seven-year budget standoff.
creator: Pieter Haeck, Marianne Gros, Gregorio Sorgi

title: Russia denies involvement in fridge hacks across Europe
content:
A spokesperson for the Kremlin denied on Thursday that Russia had any involvement in the cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigerators, calling the allegations “absurd.”

Dmitry Peskov said accusations of Russian involvement in the attacks are “unfounded,” according to reports in Russian media. These allegations are “becoming a persistent trend in European countries,” he added.

Supermarket refrigerators have been hacked in multiple European countries over the past few weeks, forcing retailers to throw away thawing fresh and frozen food. The attacks also hit French blood banks, though the country’s blood collection service said its supplies were not affected.

While pro-Russian hacker groups claimed the attacks on Wednesday, it is notoriously difficult to attribute a cyberattack to a specific actor definitively, and those groups quickly deleted the claims, according to the BBC.
snippet: A spokesperson for the Kremlin denied on Thursday that Russia had any involvement in the cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigerators, calling the allegations “absurd.”
creator: Sam Clark
